$comment: FEM part spec of the fem-gantry example (BGSimFEM): the crossbeam of an H-gantry, an aluminium box 1400 x 60 x 100 mm (length along y, width along x = the direction the gantry moves, height along z), walls 4 mm except the front wall (the rail seat), 10 mm, and 10 mm end caps. (With a 4 mm front wall the rail's torque bends the wall locally, 15 times softer, a response the reduced model only gets right at its load-mode stations.) Interface A: the first 80 mm of the beam, held in the end bracket on the X1 carriage (every surface node there, the reference frame, at the beam axis), B: the same at the X2 end. The Y carriage runs on a rail on the front wall (x = +30 mm) from y = 150 to 1250 mm. Stress hotspots on the front and back walls 100 mm from the end of the A clamp and on the back wall at mid-span, at mid-height (the extreme fibres of horizontal bending, clear of the clamp and of the rail footprint, so beam theory applies there). Run: julia --project=julia/BGSimFEM julia/BGSimFEM/bin/bgsim-fem.jl examples/fem-gantry/design/beam.fem.json
